key_insight: DiffSequence-Q uses quantum auxiliary supervision during training to guide protein diffusion design toward secondary structure requirements and solubility targets, while generation remains entirely classical.
engineering_relevance: Quantum-assisted training could improve protein design without requiring quantum hardware during sequence generation.
method: Condition multinomial diffusion on per-residue secondary structure and a continuous solubility target.
Jointly train a shared Transformer with a diffusion objective and a QNN or QKAN auxiliary solubility prediction loss.
Generate protein sequences using classical reverse diffusion.
evidence_signal: On CATH, DiffSequence-Q led four evaluated models in secondary structure recovery for complete sequence generation; the best QNN and QKAN configurations scored 14.0% and 22.7% above the MLP baseline in mean independently predicted solubility, and experiments demonstrated activity in three protein families.
watch_item: Solubility gains are predictor-based; the abstract does not establish experimental solubility improvements or a computational quantum advantage.
paper_title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
